Main.sentence: Benjamin " Bibi " Netanyahu [a] (born 21 October 1949) is an Israeli politician and diplomat who has served as ___E:Prime Minister of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel)___ since 2022. Having previously held office from 1996 to 1999 and from 2009 to 2021, Netanyahu is ___E:Israel's longest-serving prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_prime_ministers_of_Israel#Tenure_of_office_in_years)___ .
Born in ___E:Tel Aviv U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv)___ , Netanyahu was raised in ___E:West Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Jerusalem)___ and the United States.

He returned to Israel in 1967 to join the ___E:Israel Defense Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces)___ and served in the ___E:Sayeret Matkal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayeret_Matkal)___ special forces.

In 1972, he returned to the US, and after graduating from the ___E:Massachusetts Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology)___ , Netanyahu worked for the ___E:Boston Consulting Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Consulting_Group)___ .
He moved back to Israel in 1978 and founded the ___E:Yonatan Netanyahu Anti-Terror Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonatan_Netanyahu#The_Jonathan_Institute)___ .
Between 1984 and 1988 Netanyahu was ___E:Israel's ambassador to the United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%27s_ambassador_to_the_United_Nations)___ .

Netanyahu rose to prominence after his ___E:election as chair of Likud in 1993 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Likud_leadership_election)___ , becoming ___E:leader of the opposition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leader_of_the_Opposition_(Israel))___ .

In the ___E:1996 general election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Israeli_general_election)___ , Netanyahu became the first Israeli prime minister elected directly by popular vote. Netanyahu was defeated in the ___E:1999 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Israeli_general_election)___ and entered the private sector.

He returned and served as ___E:minister of foreign affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Israel))___ and ___E:finance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Finance_(Israel))___ , initiating ___E:economic reforms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_economy)___ , before resigning over the ___E:Gaza disengagement plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_disengagement_plan)___ .

Netanyahu ___E:returned to lead Likud in 2005 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Likud_leadership_election)___ , leading the opposition between 2006 and 2009. After the ___E:2009 legislative election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Israeli_legislative_election)___ , Netanyahu ___E:formed a coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty-second_government_of_Israel)___ with other right-wing parties and became prime minister again.

Netanyahu made his closeness to ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ central to his appeal from 2016. During ___E:Trump's first presidency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trump%27s_first_presidency)___ , the ___E:US recognized Jerusalem as capital of Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_recognition_of_Jerusalem_as_capital_of_Israel)___ , ___E:Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_recognition_of_the_Golan_Heights_as_part_of_Israel)___ , and brokered the ___E:Abraham Accords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Accords)___ between Israel and the ___E:Arab world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world)___ .

Netanyahu received criticism over expanding ___E:Israeli settlements U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_settlement)___ in the ___E:occupied West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupied_West_Bank)___ , deemed ___E:illegal under international law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_law_and_Israeli_settlements)___ .

In 2019, Netanyahu was ___E:indicted on charges of breach of trust, bribery and fraud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trial_of_Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ , and relinquished all ministerial posts except prime minister.

The ___E:2018–2022 Israeli political crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%932022_Israeli_political_crisis)___ resulted in a ___E:rotation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_government)___ agreement between Netanyahu and ___E:Benny Gantz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Gantz)___ .
This collapsed in 2020, leading to a ___E:2021 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Israeli_legislative_election)___ .
In June 2021, Netanyahu was removed from the premiership, before returning after the ___E:2022 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Israeli_legislative_election)___ .

Netanyahu's premierships have been criticized for perceived ___E:democratic backsliding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_backsliding)___ and an alleged shift towards authoritarianism. ___E:Netanyahu's coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirty-seventh_government_of_Israel)___ pursued ___E:judicial reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Israeli_judicial_reform)___ , which was met with ___E:large-scale protests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Israeli_judicial_reform_protests)___ in early 2023. The ___E:October 7 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks)___ by ___E:Hamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas)___ -led Palestinian groups in the same year triggered the ___E:Gaza war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war)___ , with Netanyahu facing ___E:nationwide protests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war_protests_in_Israel#"Bring_Them_Home_Now"_protests)___ for the security lapse during the attack and failure to secure the return of Israeli hostages.

In October 2024, he survived ___E:an assassination attempt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_drone_attack_on_Benjamin_Netanyahu%27s_residence)___ and ordered an ___E:invasion of Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Israeli_invasion_of_Lebanon)___ with the stated goal of destroying the military capabilities of ___E:Hezbollah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hezbollah)___ , a key ally of Hamas that ___E:helped U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93Hezbollah_conflict_(2023%E2%80%93present))___ them since the 7 October attack.

After the ___E:fall of the Assad regime U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Assad_regime)___ in December 2024, Netanyahu directed an ___E:invasion of Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Israeli_invasion_of_Syria)___ against the current ___E:Syrian government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_government)___ .
He also presided over the 2025 Israeli strikes on Iran, which escalated into the ___E:Iran–Israel war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_war)___ .

Netanyahu's government has been accused of orchestrating a ___E:genocide in Gaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide)___ , culminating in the ___E:South Africa v. Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa%27s_genocide_case_against_Israel)___ case before the ___E:International Court of Justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice)___ in December 2023. The ___E:International Criminal Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court)___ (ICC) ___E:issued an arrest warrant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court_arrest_warrants_for_Israeli_leaders)___ in November 2024 for Netanyahu for alleged ___E:war crimes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_crime)___ and ___E:crimes against humanity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes_against_humanity)___ as part of the ___E:ICC investigation in Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Criminal_Court_investigation_in_Palestine#Arrest_warrants)___ .
Netanyahu was born in 1949 in ___E:Tel Aviv U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tel_Aviv)___ .

His mother, Tzila Segal (1912–2000), was born in ___E:Petah Tikva U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petah_Tikva)___ in the Ottoman Empire's ___E:Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutasarrifate_of_Jerusalem)___ — her family had migrated from ___E:Minneapolis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minneapolis)___ in 1911, having relocated there from ___E:Lithuania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania)___ in the 1870s  — and studied law at ___E:Gray's Inn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray%27s_Inn)___ , London.

His father, ___E:Warsaw U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw)___ -born ___E:Benzion Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzion_Netanyahu)___ ( ___E:né U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%A9)___ Mileikowsky; 1910–2012), was a historian specializing in the ___E:Jewish Golden Age of Spain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_age_of_Jewish_culture_in_Spain)___ .

His paternal grandfather, ___E:Nathan Mileikowsky U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Mileikowsky)___ , was a ___E:rabbi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbi)___ and ___E:Zionist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionism)___ writer.

When Netanyahu's father immigrated to ___E:Mandatory Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine)___ , he ___E:adopted a Hebrew surname U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebraization_of_surnames)___ of "Netanyahu", meaning "God has given." While his family is predominantly ___E:Ashkenazi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews)___ , he has said that a DNA test revealed him to have some ___E:Sephardic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sephardi_Jews)___ ancestry.
He claims descent from the ___E:Vilna Gaon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilna_Gaon)___ .
Netanyahu was the second of three children.
He was initially raised and educated in ___E:Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerusalem)___ , where he attended Henrietta Szold Elementary School.

A copy of his evaluation from his 6th grade teacher Ruth Rubenstein indicated that Netanyahu was courteous, polite, and helpful; that he was "responsible and punctual"; and that he was friendly, disciplined, cheerful, brave, active, and obedient.

Between 1956 and 1958, and again from 1963 to 1967,  his family lived in the United States in ___E:Cheltenham Township, Pennsylvania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham_Township,_Pennsylvania)___ , a suburb of Philadelphia, while father Benzion Netanyahu taught at ___E:Dropsie College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dropsie_College)___ .

Benjamin attended and graduated from ___E:Cheltenham High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheltenham_High_School)___ and was active in the ___E:debate club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debate)___ , ___E:chess club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chess_club)___ , and ___E:soccer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school_soccer)___ .

He and his brother Yonatan grew dissatisfied with what they saw as the superficial way of life they encountered in the area, including the prevalent youth ___E:counterculture U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterculture)___ movement and the liberal sensibilities of the ___E:Reform U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_Judaism)___ synagogue, ___E:Temple Judea of Philadelphia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_Judea_of_Philadelphia)___ , that the family attended.
After graduating from high school in 1967, Netanyahu returned to Israel to enlist in the ___E:Israel Defense Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel_Defense_Forces)___ .
He trained as a combat soldier and served for five years in a special forces unit of the IDF, ___E:Sayeret Matkal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayeret_Matkal)___ .

He took part in numerous cross-border raids during the 1967–70 ___E:War of Attrition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Attrition)___ , including the March 1968 ___E:Battle of Karameh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Karameh)___ , when the IDF attacked ___E:Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ to capture ___E:PLO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLO)___ leader ___E:Yasser Arafat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasser_Arafat)___ but were repulsed with heavy casualties.
He became a team-leader in the unit. He was wounded in combat on multiple occasions.

He was involved in many other missions, including the ___E:1968 Israeli raid on Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Israeli_raid_on_Lebanon)___ and the rescue of the hijacked ___E:Sabena Flight 571 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabena_Flight_571)___ in May 1972, in which he was shot in the shoulder.
He was discharged from active service in 1972 but remained in the Sayeret Matkal reserves.
Following his discharge, he left to study in the United States but returned in October 1973 to serve in the ___E:Yom Kippur War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War)___ .

Netanyahu returned to the United States in late 1972 to study architecture at the ___E:Massachusetts Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts_Institute_of_Technology)___ (MIT).

After returning to Israel to fight in the Yom Kippur War, he returned to the United States and, under the name Ben Nitay , completed a ___E:bachelor's degree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science)___  in architecture  in February 1975 and earned a ___E:master's degree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master%27s_degree)___  from the ___E:MIT Sloan School of Management U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIT_Sloan_School_of_Management)___ in 1976.   Concurrently, he was studying towards a doctorate  in political science.

His studies were broken off by the death of his brother ___E:Yonatan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonatan_Netanyahu)___ who was leading the ___E:Entebbe raid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entebbe_raid)___ .

At MIT, Netanyahu studied a double-load while taking courses at ___E:Harvard University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ , completing his bachelor's degree in architecture in two and a half years, despite taking a break to fight in the Yom Kippur War. Professor Leon B. Groisser at MIT recalled: "He did superbly.
He was very bright.
Organized.
Strong.
Powerful.
He knew what he wanted to do and how to get it done."

At that time he changed his name to Benjamin " Ben " Nitai (Nitai, a reference to both ___E:Mount Nitai U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Nitai)___ and to the eponymous Jewish sage ___E:Nittai of Arbela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nittai_of_Arbela)___ , was a pen name often used by his father for articles).

Years later, in an interview with the media, Netanyahu clarified that he decided to do so to make it easier for Americans to pronounce his name. This fact has been used by his political rivals to accuse him indirectly of a lack of Israeli national identity and loyalty.

Netanyahu worked as an economic consultant  for the ___E:Boston Consulting Group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Consulting_Group)___ in Boston, Massachusetts, working at the company between 1976 and 1978. At the Boston Consulting Group, he was a colleague of ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ , with whom he formed a lasting friendship.
Romney described Netanyahu at the time as "a strong personality with a distinct point of view".
Netanyahu said that their "easy communication" was a result of "B.C.G.'s intellectually rigorous boot camp".
In 1978, Netanyahu appeared on Boston local television, under the name "Ben Nitay", where he argued: "The real core of the conflict is the unfortunate Arab refusal to accept the State of Israel ...

For 20 years the Arabs had both the West Bank and the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ , and if self-determination, as they now say, is the core of the conflict, they could have easily established a Palestinian state."
In 1978, Netanyahu returned to Israel.
Between 1978 and 1980, he ran the Jonathan Netanyahu Anti-Terror Institute,  a non-governmental organization devoted to the study of terrorism.
From 1980 to 1982, he was director of marketing for Rim Industries in Jerusalem.

___E:Moshe Arens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moshe_Arens)___ appointed him as his Deputy Chief of Mission at the Israeli Embassy in Washington, D.C., while Arens was ambassador to the United States, a position he held from 1982 until 1984.  During the ___E:1982 Lebanon War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Lebanon_War)___ , he was called up for reserve duty in Sayeret Matkal and requested to be released from service, preferring to remain in the US and serve as a spokesperson for Israel in the wake of harsh international criticism of the war. He presented Israel's case to the media during the war and established a highly efficient public relations system in the Israeli embassy.
Between 1984 and 1988, Netanyahu served as the ___E:Israeli ambassador to the United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_ambassador_to_the_United_Nations)___ .
Netanyahu was influenced by Rabbi ___E:Menachem M. Schneerson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_M._Schneerson)___ , with whom he formed a relationship during the 1980s.
He referred to Schneerson as "the most influential man of our time".

Also during the 1980s, Netanyahu became friends with ___E:Fred Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Trump)___ , the father of future U.S. president ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ .

Prior to the ___E:1988 Israeli legislative election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Israeli_legislative_election)___ , Netanyahu returned to Israel and joined the ___E:Likud U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Likud)___ party.

In the Likud's internal elections, Netanyahu was placed fifth on the party list. Later on he was elected as a Knesset member of the 12th Knesset, and was appointed as a deputy of the foreign minister ___E:Moshe Arens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moshe_Arens)___ , and later on ___E:David Levy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Levy_(Israeli_politician))___ .
Netanyahu and Levy did not cooperate and the rivalry between the two only intensified afterwards.

During the ___E:Gulf War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War)___ in early 1991, the English-fluent Netanyahu emerged as the principal spokesman for Israel in media interviews on ___E:CNN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN)___ and other news outlets.

During the ___E:Madrid Conference of 1991 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid_Conference_of_1991)___ Netanyahu was a member of the Israeli delegation headed by Prime Minister ___E:Yitzhak Shamir U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Shamir)___ .
After the Madrid Conference Netanyahu was appointed as Deputy Minister in the Israeli Prime Minister's Office.

Following the defeat of the Likud party in the ___E:1992 Israeli legislative elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Israeli_legislative_election)___ the Likud party ___E:held a party leadership election in 1993 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Likud_leadership_election)___ , and Netanyahu was victorious, defeating ___E:Benny Begin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benny_Begin)___ , son of the late prime minister ___E:Menachem Begin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_Begin)___ , and veteran politician David Levy  (Sharon initially sought Likud party leadership as well, but quickly withdrew when it was evident that he was attracting minimal support).
Shamir retired from politics shortly after the Likud's defeat in the 1992 elections.

Following the ___E:assassination of Yitzhak Rabin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Yitzhak_Rabin)___ at the end of a rally in support of the ___E:Oslo Accords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_Accords)___ , ___E:Rabin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin)___ 's temporary successor ___E:Shimon Peres U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimon_Peres)___ decided to call early elections in order to give the government a mandate to advance the peace process.

Netanyahu was the Likud's candidate for prime minister in the ___E:1996 Israeli legislative election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Israeli_prime_ministerial_election)___ which took place on 29 May 1996 and were the first Israeli elections in which ___E:Israelis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israelis)___ elected their prime minister directly.
Netanyahu hired American political operative ___E:Arthur Finkelstein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_J._Finkelstein)___ to run his campaign.

Netanyahu won the ___E:1996 election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Israeli_prime_ministerial_election)___ , becoming the youngest person in the history of the position and the first Israeli prime minister to be born in the State of Israel ( ___E:Yitzhak Rabin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yitzhak_Rabin)___ was born in Jerusalem, under the British Mandate of Palestine, prior to the 1948 founding of the Israeli state).

Netanyahu's victory over the pre-election favorite ___E:Shimon Peres U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimon_Peres)___ surprised many. The main catalyst in the downfall of the latter was a wave of ___E:suicide bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Palestinian_suicide_attacks)___ shortly before the elections; on ___E:3 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaffa_Road_bus_bombings#Second_bombing)___ and ___E:4 March 1996 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dizengoff_Center_suicide_bombing)___ , Palestinians carried out two ___E:suicide bombings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_bombing)___ , killing 32 Israelis, with Peres seemingly unable to stop the attacks.

During the campaign, Netanyahu stressed that progress in the peace process would be based on the ___E:Palestinian National Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_National_Authority)___ fulfilling its obligations – mainly fighting terrorism – and the Likud campaign slogan was, "Netanyahu – making a safe peace".

Although Netanyahu won the election for prime minister, Peres's ___E:Israeli Labor Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Labor_Party)___ received more seats in the ___E:Knesset elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Israeli_legislative_election)___ .

Netanyahu had to rely on a coalition with the ___E:ultra-Orthodox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haredi_Judaism)___ parties, ___E:Shas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shas)___ and ___E:UTJ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Torah_Judaism)___ in order to form a government.
The months leading up to the 1996 Israeli election were marred by a series of ___E:Hamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas)___ terrorist attacks in Israel.
